user.title: Manual J
user.description: What a part in House Structure that gives no value of its own is taken to be, and the outdoor sensor the design temperatures come from.

data_description.outdoor_entity: The design temperatures come from its recorded hourly means over the last two years. Without one, assumed design temperatures for Edmonton are used.
data_description.infiltration_ach: Natural air changes per hour, for the loads. Leave empty for 0.35, a fairly tight house; an older house is often 0.5 to 0.7. From a blower-door test, roughly ACH50 divided by 20.
data_description.wall_r: The effective R-value of the outside walls, studs included (R-20 batts in 2x6 framing are about R-15 overall). Leave empty for R-20. A wall part in House Structure with its own R-value keeps it.
data_description.roof_r: The effective R-value of the ceilings under the roof. Leave empty for R-35. A roof part with its own R-value keeps it.
data_description.door_r: The R-value of the doors to outside, with their frames. Leave empty for R-3, an insulated steel or solid wood door. A glass patio door is better entered as a window in House Structure.
data_description.basement_floor_r: The basement slab and the soil under it, as one effective R-value against the design ground temperature. Leave empty for R-11, an uninsulated slab.
